---
title: "Research Guide"
format:
  html:
    embed-resources: true
    page-layout: full
    toc: false
execute:
  keep-md: true
params:
  dgf_file: "DGF.xlsx"
  data_file: null
---

<!-- datagoodr research guide template ("compact" style).

     The same guide as the default "rail" template, condensed for
     documentation: each variable is still a unit with a left rail (data type,
     label, name, description) and a right column, but PROPERTIES is a one-row
     strip, the preview and the long tables are kept short, the graphics are
     drawn smaller, and the whitespace is roughly halved -- several variables
     to a screen instead of one. Nothing is left out.

     For the taller default guide use create_rg(style = "rail"), and for the
     original three-column grid create_rg(style = "vintage").

     Customize without editing the package:
       - DG.R                   custom functions & layout overrides
       - datagoodr-compact.css  fonts, colors and spacing
     See vignette("report-aesthetics", package = "datagoodr").

     Render from the console with:  quarto::quarto_render("research-guide.qmd")
     or re-render against a different DGF/dataset without editing this file:
       datagoodr::update_rg("research-guide.qmd", DGF = "DGF-V2.xlsx") -->

```{r setup, include=FALSE}

# datagoodr is the only package this report needs to attach. Everything it
# renders is a datagoodr function, and those load what they need themselves.
library( datagoodr )

# Source the project customization file (custom functions / layout overrides)
# if it sits next to this document.
if( file.exists("DG.R") ) source("DG.R")

# The DGF drives the whole report. The path comes from the `dgf_file` param, so
# this document renders on its own - and update_rg() can point it at a
# different DGF at render time without editing this file.
dgf <- load_dgf( params$dgf_file, reader = "readxl" )

# Optional raw dataset. The report renders from the DGF alone - every statistic
# and graphic is already stored in its rg_* columns - so this stays NULL unless
# a caller supplies `data_file`. When supplied it is read once here and left
# available to DG.R and to any custom chunk that needs the underlying values.
raw.data <- if( is.null( params$data_file ) ) NULL else
            suppressMessages( readr::read_csv( params$data_file ) )

# One group per report template (dg_render_type), in display order. Each group
# gets its own chunk below because each graphic needs its own fig size.
groups <- rail_groups( dgf )
```

```{r contents, echo=FALSE, results="asis"}
rail_contents( groups )
```

```{r boolean, echo=FALSE, results="asis", fig.width=8, fig.height=1.35}
rail_sections( groups$Boolean, "Boolean", style = "compact" )
```

```{r categorical, echo=FALSE, results="asis", fig.width=8, fig.height=2.2}
rail_sections( groups$Categorical, "Categorical", style = "compact" )
```

```{r numeric, echo=FALSE, results="asis", fig.width=8, fig.height=1.5}
rail_sections( groups$Numeric, "Numeric", style = "compact" )
```

```{r text, echo=FALSE, results="asis", fig.width=8, fig.height=2.2}
rail_sections( groups$Text, "Text", style = "compact" )
```

```{r identifier, echo=FALSE, results="asis"}
rail_sections( groups$Identifier, "Identifier", style = "compact" )
```

```{r temporal, echo=FALSE, results="asis", fig.width=8, fig.height=2.6}
rail_sections( groups$Temporal, "Temporal", style = "compact" )
```

```{r datagoodr-style, echo=FALSE, results="asis"}
# The report stylesheet comes from a single source: datagoodr-compact.css (a
# local copy overrides the packaged one). Edit that file to restyle the report.
cat( "<style>\n", datagoodr_css("compact"), "\n</style>\n" )
```

```{r datagoodr-record, echo=FALSE, results="asis"}
# Provenance for this render - which DGF produced this file, its content hash,
# package/R/quarto versions, and when. Written as an HTML comment, so it travels
# with the report without appearing in it; read it back with
# datagoodr::read_render_record("research-guide.html").
#
#   visible  = TRUE  also prints it as a table in the report
#   identify = TRUE  adds your username and absolute paths. Off by default:
#                    this file is meant to be shared.
render_record( dgf, params$dgf_file, params$data_file )
```
